title: Seven Franchises Want Him. Hardik Pandya's Mumbai Indians Chapter Is Heading for Its Final Page.
excerpt: Only RCB and SRH are sitting this one out. From CSK to KKR to Rajasthan Royals, the most contested IPL trade in years is shaping up — and the off-season drama is just getting started.
body:
The numbers were always going to force the conversation. Nine wins in the last two IPL seasons. A ninth-place finish in 2026 — Mumbai Indians' worst ever. Four wins, ten defeats, elimination confirmed by May 10. And at the centre of it all, Hardik Pandya, the captain who was supposed to herald a new era.

Now, according to a Times of India report, seven of the IPL's ten franchises have expressed interest in acquiring the 32-year-old all-rounder. Only Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Sunrisers Hyderabad have opted out. Everyone else — Chennai Super Kings, Kolkata Knight Riders, Rajasthan Royals, Lucknow Super Giants, Delhi Capitals, Punjab Kings, and Gujarat Titans — is in the conversation.

It is the most hotly contested trade scenario in IPL history. And it says as much about the league's evolving power dynamics as it does about the complicated legacy of Pandya himself.

## The MI Experiment That Never Worked

Pandya's return to Mumbai Indians ahead of IPL 2024 was supposed to be a homecoming. Instead, it became a three-year cautionary tale about chemistry, captaincy, and the cost of disrupting a winning formula. The decision to replace Rohit Sharma as captain — still one of the most polarising calls in franchise cricket history — never sat well with the Wankhede faithful.

In IPL 2026, Pandya managed 206 runs in ten matches at a strike rate of 138 and picked up just four wickets at an economy of 11.43. The all-rounder who once won India a T20 World Cup with his death bowling was a shadow of that version. MI's middle-order collapse became a weekly ritual, and the captaincy burden only seemed to deepen the slump.

Pandya has since relocated to the BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, making it his permanent training base — a quiet signal that his Mumbai chapter may already be over in all but paperwork.

## Who Wants Him — And What They'd Give Up

The frontrunners tell you everything about where the IPL's power is shifting.

**Kolkata Knight Riders** and **Rajasthan Royals** were the first to signal interest. KKR, fresh off their 2024 title under Shreyas Iyer (who has since moved on to India's T20I captaincy), want a marquee all-rounder to anchor their next cycle. RR's interest is more intriguing — reports suggest they could offer Yashasvi Jaiswal in a blockbuster swap, a move that would reshape both franchises overnight.

**Chennai Super Kings** entering the race adds a layer of strategic intrigue. With MS Dhoni's influence waning and the franchise planning its post-Dhoni identity, Pandya as a potential captain-leader-all-rounder fits CSK's template perfectly. Former India spinner R. Ashwin — now a franchise cricket analyst as much as an active player — has mapped out trade scenarios on his YouTube channel, suggesting MI would only agree to a CSK deal if it included emerging star Ayush Mhatre.

**Lucknow Super Giants** represent perhaps the most logical fit. Former India opener Aakash Chopra has publicly floated a deal that would send Nicholas Pooran and Mohsin Khan to Mumbai in exchange for Pandya — addressing LSG's desperate need for an Indian all-rounder while giving MI two quality overseas and domestic options.

## Why This Matters Beyond the Boardroom

For the estimated 50 million NRI cricket fans who follow the IPL from living rooms in New Jersey, living rooms in London, and watch parties in the Bay Area, trade season has become the off-season's main event. The IPL window — which runs through July and August before the 2027 auction cycle — has turned franchise cricket's back office into appointment viewing.

The Pandya trade is the centrepiece because it forces every franchise to answer the same question: what are you building toward? KKR wants a proven winner. RR wants a captain. CSK wants a bridge to its next decade. LSG wants balance. Each trade package reveals a franchise's self-assessment more honestly than any press conference.

And for Pandya himself, the trade represents something rarer: a second reinvention. He has already gone from T20 World Cup hero to MI captain to fallen leader. A fresh franchise — a new city, a new set of expectations — could be the reset that saves a career that still has five or six elite years left in it.

## The Clock Is Ticking

The IPL trade window will close before the 2027 auction preparations begin in earnest. MI's front office, led by franchise owner Nita Ambani's trusted inner circle, has reportedly not ruled out retaining Pandya — but the weight of evidence suggests they are testing the market.

One thing is clear: whatever franchise Pandya suits up for in March 2027, the move will redefine the league's competitive landscape. In a competition that has become the world's most-watched T20 league, the Pandya trade is this off-season's defining storyline. And with seven bidders already circling, the final act is likely to be as dramatic as anything on the field.
